prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
As of September 2026, a quiet tension is appearing in how young people in Japan think about travel. Many, especially young men, want trips they can shape for themselves. But the stays measured in surveys are still short.

Different surveys point to this wish. In a 2025 survey, men aged 29 and under chose solo travel at 25.2% and hobby-focused travel at 24.3%. These were two of their leading choices.

But the picture changes when we look at travel length. When people imagined having one full month off, “about one week” was the most popular answer, at 24.1%. In an autumn survey, planned stays averaged 1.8 nights, with 2.0 nights as the middle answer.

One report also lists longer stays as a task for Japan. So this is not a simple story of young people moving from famous sightseeing spots to long, slow holidays.

It is a story about a gap. The wish for more personal time is growing, but longer stays have not yet become normal behavior. The pattern also differs by gender: 44.7% of women aged 29 and under were interested in visiting famous tourist spots.

【Point One】
Slow travel does not always mean staying for many nights. Among men under 29, solo travel and hobby-focused travel were both leading choices. In another survey, about 90% of Japanese Gen Z respondents wanted free time on an overseas tour, and about 80% wanted half a day or more. The common wish is control over time, not only a longer calendar.

【Point Two】
Here is the harder part: wanting a longer trip is not the same as being able to take one. With a full month off, “about one week” was the most common choice. But autumn travel plans averaged 1.8 nights, with 2.0 nights as the middle answer. The report links travel with time and money. A slow-travel message alone may not be enough; longer stays need enough time and money.

point_one.reasoning: Full Storyにない、海外ツアーで自由時間を求めるGen Zの具体的な数値を加え、旅行の志向を宿泊日数ではなく時間の裁量として捉え直している。若者の旅行需要を「長期滞在」だけで測れないという具体的な示唆があり、聞き手の理解を深める。

point_two.reasoning: Full Storyと同じ数値を再提示しているが、単なる希望と実際に旅行できる能力を区別し、時間と費用が長期滞在の障壁になるという説明を加えている。長期滞在を促すメッセージだけでは行動変化につながらないという、政策・旅行事業者にも関わる具体的な示唆がある。
